# Headway

> Headway Ag LLC builds solar ear tags that hold a virtual fence for livestock, and one ranch app for grazing, the herd, money and tax. The app has no subscription. Tags are in testing. Patent pending. Contact: hughheadwayag@gmail.com

## Key facts

- Product: Three solar ear tags that hold a virtual fence, and one app for the whole place
- Livestock: All livestock
- Worn as: An ear tag, not a collar
- Power: Charged by the sun. Built to last 15 years
- Fence: Sound first. A stimulus only as a last step
- Health: Heart rate, temperature, blood oxygen and movement on every animal
- Land and wildlife: Pictures of grass and plants, bird and insect life, predator alerts
- Also does: Moves, splits and guides the herd. Lightning and problem alerts. Weight records with a walk-over scale
- App: Map, grazing, herd records, money and tax. No subscription
- Status: Tags in testing. Patent pending
- Contact: hughheadwayag@gmail.com

## How virtual fencing for livestock works | Headway

URL: https://headwayfence.com/virtual-fencing/

How virtual fencing for livestock works | Headway
Skip to the page
How a virtual fence works
Draw the line on a map. The tags hold it. A tone warns first.
1
Draw it
Draw a paddock, a strip or a keep-out zone on the map. It goes to every tag in the mob.
2
Warn it
As an animal walks toward the line, its tag plays a tone. Most turn back right there.
3
Hold it
If it keeps going, the tone gets stronger. A stimulus is the last step, with strict limits.
Fence anything in or out.
Grazing strips, creek banks, water points and pivot towers, all from the map. Choosing where stock graze, and for how long, builds better soil and better grass.
A virtual fence does not replace your boundary and road fences.
Photo: Photo by Bob Nichols, USDA Natural Resources Conservation Service. , Public domain , resized

## Virtual fencing and animal welfare | Headway

URL: https://headwayfence.com/virtual-fencing/welfare.html

Virtual fencing and animal welfare | Headway
Skip to the page
Animal welfare comes first
Sound does the work. A stimulus is only a last step.
Sound first
A tone always comes first. Most animals turn back on the tone.
Never on the way back
An animal heading back in is never cued.
Not while running
A scared or running animal is left alone.
Strict limits
Only a few cues a day, with rest between them.
Out too far
The tag goes quiet and tells you where the animal is.
Not sure, no cue
If the tag is not sure where it is, it does nothing.
These rules are built into the tag. Nobody can switch them off.

## How to choose a virtual fence for livestock | Headway

URL: https://headwayfence.com/virtual-fencing/choosing.html

How to choose a virtual fence for livestock | Headway
Skip to the page
How to choose a virtual fence
Questions to ask any company before you buy, and how Headway answers them.
What does it cost each year?
The app has no subscription. The tags run on a cost-effective subscription.
Does it keep working on cloudy days?
Yes. The tags are charged by the sun and the fence holds.
Does it work with no cell signal?
Yes. Each tag keeps the fence and the grazing plan on its own.
Can I keep stock off a creek or the yard?
Yes, with as many keep-out zones as you need.
Can I turn it off while I feed?
Yes. Pause a mob from the app, and turn it back on when you are done.
What if an animal gets out?
The tag goes quiet and shows you where it is.
Is it worn on the neck or the ear?
The ear. No collar to snap or catch.
Is the app only for phones?
No. It is made for computer and tablet, and works on a phone.
Does it help with the rest of the place?
Yes. Grazing plans, herd records, money and tax are in the same app.
Before you buy
Ask to talk to people who use it.
Ask what changes when you renew.
Ask what else you have to buy, such as towers, base stations or data plans.

## Solar livestock ear tag for virtual fencing | Headway

Solar livestock ear tag for virtual fencing | Headway

The Headway ear tag
Know where every animal is and how it is doing. You only hear about it when it matters.
The herd tag, camera tag and lead tag, from our CAD model.
An ear tag, not a collar.
It goes in the ear like the tags you already use. No neck strap to stretch, snap or catch on a fence.
Three tags, one herd
Herd tag
Goes on every animal. Holds the fence and watches heart rate, temperature and movement.
Lead tag
Goes in the other ear of a few animals. Finds the herd on the map, sends news to your app and hears lightning.
Camera tag
Goes in the other ear of a few animals. Takes pictures of the grass, plants and wildlife where the herd grazes.
Where they are
Every animal on your map.
How they are doing
Heart rate, temperature and blood oxygen, plus grazing, resting and walking.
Heat stress
Know when the herd is getting too hot.
Off on its own

Not moving
Goes straight to the top of your list.
Leaving the place
If animals move fast off your place, you know right away.
Lightning
Know when a storm is close.
Your own alerts
Set your own, like a cow going off alone to calve.
Lost contact

Every angle
Sun side, from above.
From the back.
Straight down on the solar cells.

## Virtual fencing questions answered | Headway

URL: https://headwayfence.com/faq.html

Virtual fencing questions answered | Headway
Skip to the page
Questions about Headway
What is Headway?
Solar ear tags that act as a fence you draw on a map, plus one app for grazing, the herd, money and tax.
What is virtual fencing?
You draw the fence on a map. When an animal walks toward the line, its tag plays a tone and it turns back. No posts, no wire.
Is it a legal boundary fence?
No. Keep your boundary and road fences. Headway is for moving and holding stock inside your place.
Does it hurt the animals?
Sound does the work. A stimulus is only a last step, with strict limits. Animals walking back or running are left alone.
Why an ear tag and not a collar?
No neck strap to stretch, snap or catch on a fence.
How is the tag powered?
It is charged by the sun. It is sealed and built to last 15 years.
What if there is no cell signal?
The tags keep the fence and the grazing plan on their own.
Can it warn me about lightning?
Yes. The app tells you when a storm is getting close to the herd.
What does it cost?
The app has no subscription. The tags run on a cost-effective subscription. Prices come before the first sale.
Which animals does it work with?
All livestock: cattle, sheep, goats and more.
Which tag goes on which animal?
The herd tag goes on every animal. A few animals in each herd also wear a lead tag or a camera tag in the other ear.
When does an animal get its tag?
Its record starts the day it is born, linked to its mother. The Headway tag goes on at weaning, when the ear is big enough.
Can it tell if an animal is sick?
The herd tag tracks heart rate, temperature, blood oxygen and how the animal moves. When one of them drifts from that animal's normal, you get an alert, often before you could see it.
Can it watch for predators?
Yes. The tags listen for wolves, coyotes and dogs, and notice when the herd bunches up or runs. You get an alert with where it happened.
Can it tell me about my land?
Yes. Camera tags take pictures of the grass and plants as the herd grazes, and every tag listens for birds and insects. Over time you see your land getting better, or not.
How does it save me time?
No fence to build or move, moves that happen on their own, and one list of today's jobs with the most urgent first.
Does the tag weigh animals?
No. It works with a walk-over scale, so each weight saves to the right animal on its own.
Can a vet see records in the field?
Yes. Hold a phone to the tag and the record opens.
Which tax forms does it fill in?
The farm tax form for the country you are in. The United States first, then Canada, Australia and England. Your accountant checks and files.
When can I buy tags?
Tags are in testing now. Get in touch and we will keep you posted.
How do I contact Headway?
Email hughheadwayag@gmail.com.
Want Headway on your place?
Our first ranches are already lined up. Tell us about yours.
Get in touch Questions

## Privacy and cookie choice on headwayfence.com

URL: https://headwayfence.com/privacy.html

Privacy and cookie choice on headwayfence.com
Skip to the page
Privacy and cookie choice
What headwayfence.com counts, what it stores in your browser, and how to change your mind.
What this site counts
Page views only: a number for each page and each day. No cookies, no names, no email addresses, no location. There is no account and no login.
Nothing here follows you around the web. This site runs no ads.
What the Accept button adds
Press Accept and one small flag is saved in this browser, so a repeat visit is counted once a day. It has no name attached. It is not a cookie and it is not sent to any advertiser.
How to opt out
Press Essential only and no flag is saved. If you pressed Accept and changed your mind, clear this site's data in your browser and the banner will ask again.
What is never collected
No name, address, phone number, password or card number. Email only reaches us when you choose to send it.
Questions
Write to hughheadwayag@gmail.com if anything here is unclear.

## Automatic livestock weight records | Headway

Automatic livestock weight records | Headway
Skip to the page
Automatic weight records
The tag does not weigh. It works with a walk-over scale, so every weight saves to the right animal with no typing.
How it works
Put a walk-over scale in the lane to water. The scale is bought separately.
Pick how often to weigh.
On weigh days the herd is guided through the scale lane.
Each weight lands on that animal's record.
Photo: USDA NRCS Texas , Public domain , resized
Daily gain
See how fast each animal is gaining.
Falling behind
An animal that stops gaining shows up first. That is often the first sign of trouble.
Sell on time
See which animals are at target weight.

## Heart rate and temperature on every animal | Headway

URL: https://headwayfence.com/ear-tag/health.html

Heart rate and temperature on every animal | Headway
Skip to the page
Health monitoring
The herd tag watches every animal, day and night. You hear about it when something changes.
Heart rate
A heart rate that climbs or drops from that animal's normal is often the first sign of trouble.
Temperature
Spot a fever early, before the animal goes off its feed.
Blood oxygen
Another early sign when an animal is not right.
Movement
Grazing, resting and walking each day. Less grazing or more lying down shows up fast.
Heat stress
The tag feels the heat and humidity around the herd, and warns you before it gets dangerous.
Your own alerts
Set alerts for what matters to you, like a cow going off alone to calve.
Catch it early
Each animal has its own normal. Headway learns it, and tells you when that animal drifts from it. You check the one that needs you, not the whole herd.
Every reading goes on the animal's record, ready for your vet.
Photo: USDAgov , Public domain , resized

## Land and wildlife monitoring from the herd | Headway

URL: https://headwayfence.com/ear-tag/wildlife.html

Land and wildlife monitoring from the herd | Headway
Skip to the page
Land and wildlife
Your herd walks every corner of your place. Their tags see and hear it, so you know what is living on your land.
Grass and plants
Camera tags take pictures of the ground as the herd grazes. See grass cover, bare ground and which plants are coming in.
Weeds
Spot a weed patch early, and drop it on today's job list.
Birds
Every tag listens. Bird song tells you which birds live on your land, and how that changes year to year.
Insects
Hear the buzz of bees, crickets and other insects. More life in the grass is a sign of healthy land.
Predators
The tags listen for wolves, coyotes and dogs, and notice when the herd bunches up or runs. You get an alert and where it happened.
Other wildlife
Deer, hogs and other animals the camera tags catch, marked on your map.
See your land get better
Good grazing brings more grass, more plants, more birds and more insects. Headway keeps a record of all of it, season by season, paddock by paddock.
A map of what lives where.
A yearly report for your land.
Proof of the good you are doing, for buyers, programs and the next generation.

Reminders

## Livestock health, breeding and lifetime records | Headway

URL: https://headwayfence.com/software/records.html

Livestock health, breeding and lifetime records | Headway
Skip to the page
Health, breeding and lifetime records
Every animal's story in one place, from the day it is born to the day it sells.
From birth
A calf's record starts the day it is born, linked to its mother. Its Headway tag goes on at weaning.
Family lines
Mother, father and breed on every animal.
Health
Vaccines and treatments, with withdrawal dates worked out for you.
Weights
Birth, weaning and every weight since.
Behaviour
An alert when an animal stops acting like itself.
Moves
Every paddock it has been in.
Ready for the vet and the buyer
Pull up the history in the field, or print it for a buyer, a vet or a breed registry.
Your records are yours. Export everything any time.

## Ranch and virtual fencing words explained | Headway

URL: https://headwayfence.com/glossary.html

Ranch and virtual fencing words explained | Headway
Skip to the page
Words we use
Plain meanings for the words on this site and in the Headway app.
Virtual fence A fence drawn on a map in an app and held by a tag on each animal, with sound first instead of wire and posts. Strip A smaller part of a paddock that a mob grazes for a short time before moving on. Strip grazing Giving the herd a fresh strip of grass every day or two, with a back fence so grazed ground can rest. Mob A group of animals managed together, such as cows and calves or a group of steers. Paddock A fenced or virtually fenced area of pasture. Keep-out zone An area inside a paddock that animals are kept out of, such as a creek bank or the yard. Rest period Days since a paddock was last grazed. Good rest lets grass grow back. Stocking rate How many animals the land carries. Grazing days How many days a strip or paddock can feed a mob. Holistic Management A way of planning that looks at people, money and land together. Walk-over scale A scale in a lane, often on the way to water, that weighs each animal as it walks across. Daily gain How much weight an animal puts on each day. Withdrawal period Days after a treatment before an animal can be sold for meat or its milk used. Tone The sound a Headway tag plays as an animal walks toward the fence line. Most animals turn back on the tone. Stimulus The last step at the fence line, used only after the tones, with strict limits.
